text:
emma: Quick sketch — thinking about a single 'sweep' chart we can use across blog post, launch post, and webinar slides to tell the latency vs unit-cost story for SMB vs Enterprise slices. TL;DR: show latency on x, $/k tokens on y, shade preferred SLA regions, draw arrows for batching & quantization impact.

raj: Love the mental model. Can we make it clear for non-technical PMs? maybe add a simple 2-line caption and a legend that ties to product levers (batching, cache, quant) so calls-to-action map to features.

lisa: +1. Also want a small inset that shows "expected ROI" numbers for sample customer (chatbot with 500k tokens/mo). Keeps it concrete for inbound leads.

mike: hmm what about variant routing? we should annotate where Dedicated / Private / Hosted fit on the sweep so sales can route leads. Hosted = lower cost / higher latency area sometimes, Dedicated = lower latency slice.

emma: good call. my rough layout: main sweep (latency x / $ y), 3 colored zones: green (SLA-safe), amber (acceptable w/ config), red (risky). overlay arrows for batching and quantization showing downward cost movement. legend with 4 icons: Hosted, Dedicated, Private, Optimize (batch/cache). caption: "Pick the right tradeoff — lower latency costs more; Redwood offers levers to shift your app left/down the curve."

raj: can you paste a tiny ascii mock so design has something to riff on?

emma: sure — quick ascii: 
```
      $/k tokens
         ^
         |      [green zone]
         |    \  /    [arrow: batching -> down]
         |     \/
         |-----+------------------> latency ms
         |     /\   [arrow: quant -> down]
         |    /  \  [amber zone]
         | [red zone]
```

lisa: perfect. for messaging: headline option A: "Control latency, cut cost: actionable levers for inference". Headline B: "Latency isn't binary — tune for your SLA and unit economics". Which feels more launchy?

mike: A is punchier for a post, B works as webinar subtitle. Also consider a short CTA for inbound routing: "Share your tokens & SLA — we'll recommend a config and expected TCO". That can be an inbound form field.

emma: routing notes: we can add three lead buckets in post/webinar: Trial (self-serve + Hosted playbook), Committed (Dedicated sizing/quote), Regulated (Private + compliance). Use a tiny flow diagram in workshop slide and link to intake form.

raj: for charts — ask design for 3 export pngs: hero sweep (wide), small inset ROI table, and simplified 1-column slide showing "how to move left/down" steps. Deadline: first pass by EOD Friday so content can sync with webinar dry run next Tue.

lisa: I'll write the 2-line caption and the sample ROI calc (need avg tokens/session, sessions/mo). pinging ops-bot for a sample usage profile later.

ops-bot: @lisa I can fetch anonymized usage buckets. run `usage_fetch --bucket smb_chatbot --last 30d` and paste results.

lisa: thanks — will grab and populate ROI numbers tomorrow morning.

mike: design note — avoid log scales unless we annotate carefully. reviewers will misread. keep axes linear and call out any compression.

emma: noted. also want one slide that explicitly ties each quadrant to a sales play and a one-line pitch. I'll draft that after design has the charts.

raj: small copy ask: include one sentence about fallbacks (auto-routing to cheaper model variant under load) — that's a key reliability differentiation for enterprise buyers.

emma: added. final checklist: 1) design: sweep + inset + flow (due Fri EOD) 2) copy: headline A/B, 2-line caption, quadrant sales blurbs (Lisa + Emma) 3) webinar: two slides (hero + playbook) + 30s demo notes (Mike) 4) inbound: intake form fields + routing rules (Raj) 5) publish plan: blog post + one-page launch post + webinar registration CTA (Marketing ops). any blockers?

lisa: none from copy side.

mike: no blockers, will prep demo clips.

emma: cool — I'll create a figma file and drop link here when ready. thanks team :thumbsup:

ops-bot: @emma figma space created: https://figma.com/s/redwood/sweepchart-launch (share link set to team)

emma: awesome — linking into the deck repo now.

raj: great work. i'll schedule a 30-min sync after design drops assets.

mike: +1.

emma: closing thread — will post updates in #marketing as assets appear.
